forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: Stage 1 complaints completed on time at 65.06% against 90% target; Stage 2 at 82% against 90% target
findings.detail: Complaint handling performance remains below target. Stage 1 complaints are completed on time in 65.06% of cases (target 90%), and Stage 2 in 82% of cases (target 90%). The council reports significant improvement compared to the prior year, with reduced response times and a new CRM system introduced in the latter stages of the year.
findings.matters: Complaint handling indicates management capacity and service quality. While below-target performance could suggest resource or process issues, the positive trend and system improvements indicate management action and suggest this is being actively addressed.
findings.figures: Stage 1: 65.06% vs 90% target (25-point gap); Stage 2: 82% vs 90% target (8-point gap)
findings.quote: % of stage 1 complaints completed on time 65.06%Target: 90%

findings.headline: Residential rent arrears at 3.51% of annual income, below 4.55% target; former tenant arrears reduced to £950K
findings.detail: The Income Recovery dashboard shows current residential rent arrears at 3.51% of projected annual income, below the 4.55% target. Former tenant arrears have reduced from £1.1M to £0.95M following introduction of dedicated recovery resources in January 2026. The council wrote off £260K during the year, including £220K in statute-barred debt.
findings.matters: Rent collection performance is fundamental to HRA financial viability and the council's capacity to service debt. Strong collection performance particularly during welfare system transition demonstrates effective income recovery management and control over the primary revenue stream.
findings.figures: Current arrears: 3.51% vs 4.55% target; Current value: £1.11M; Former tenant arrears: £0.95M (down from £1.1M); Debt written off: £0.26M
findings.quote: The Income Recovery team has exceeded their target by keeping current rent arrears at 3.51%, well below the 4.55% KPI. This is a strong result given the continued transition from Housing Benefit to Universal Credit, which can initially place tenants into arrears.

findings.headline: 279 dwellings with overdue electrical installation condition reports; domestic EICR compliance at 94.37% against 100% target
findings.detail: Domestic EICR (electrical installation condition report) compliance stands at 94.37% against a 100% target, representing 279 dwellings with overdue inspections. The council has implemented a new door-knocking process to gain access to older properties. Compliance has been increasing slowly.
findings.matters: Electrical safety certification is a legal compliance requirement. A backlog of 279 overdue inspections represents both safety risks to tenants and potential legal and reputational exposure. It may also indicate asset management or operational capacity issues.
findings.quote: we still have 279 dwellings with an overdue EICR, we have put a new door knocking process into place to try and help gain access to some of the oldest overdue properties

findings.headline: Sureserve gas repairs contractor underperforming: emergency repairs 87.83% on time against 98% target
findings.detail: Sureserve's performance on gas repairs is below target across multiple KPIs: emergency repairs at 87.83% on time (target 98%), urgent repairs at 92.57% (target 98%), and routine repairs at 91.72% (target 100%). The council commentary notes the contractor faced challenges from a Swale Heating acquisition and restructuring, and an action plan has been implemented.
findings.matters: Emergency repair underperformance raises safety concerns and impacts tenant satisfaction. Contractor underperformance indicates the council may face service delivery issues or need to enforce contractual terms, raising questions about contract management effectiveness and value for money.
findings.figures: Emergency repairs: 87.83% vs 98% target; Urgent repairs: 92.57% vs 98% target; Routine repairs: 91.72% vs 100% target
findings.quote: Their KPIs and contractual performance has not been where we would like them to be during 25/26 and we have worked with them on an action plan to address these issues.

findings.headline: Contractual invoices paid on time at 72.38% against 99% target
findings.detail: The Capital Spend dashboard shows that only 72.38% of contractual invoices are being paid on time, significantly below the 99% target. This represents a substantial gap in a key financial control metric.
findings.matters: Late invoice payment can indicate cash flow problems, administrative failures, or control weaknesses. It damages supplier relationships, may increase costs, and suggests the governance or administration issues that external lenders and auditors view as early-stage warning signs.
findings.figures: 72.38% on time; Target: 99%; Gap: 26.62 percentage points
findings.quote: % of contractual invoices paid on time 72.38%Target: 99%
